openai.feedback:
1. **Category:** approach  **Severity:** high  **Finding:** charter.md is never written in the first draft.  **Suggestion:** write it as part of a single server-side commit endpoint, ordered before daemon-config.json/org-chart.json.
2. **Category:** correctness  **Severity:** high  **Finding:** the verdict's daemonConfig is client-assembled from scratch instead of a fresh read of the real file.  **Suggestion:** expose a server-side fresh-read-and-merge via a new GET .../daemon-config route.
3. **Category:** approach  **Severity:** high  **Finding:** the three writes are client-sequenced with no atomicity or recovery story.  **Suggestion:** collapse into one ordered, partially-idempotent server commit endpoint.
4. **Category:** correctness  **Severity:** medium  **Finding:** the action->allowed_skills mapping guesses from an action id instead of using the action catalog's own slash_command field.  **Suggestion:** read slash_command directly.
5. **Category:** edge-case  **Severity:** low  **Finding:** legacy non-kebab-case domains and Windows-path-form edge cases are not handled in the absolute-path guard.  **Suggestion:** add explicit, tested cases for both.

glm.feedback:
1. **Category:** approach  **Severity:** high  **Finding:** charter.md is missing from the write sequence.  **Suggestion:** same as openai -- write it server-side as part of the ordered commit.
2. **Category:** approach  **Severity:** high  **Finding:** the three writes have no atomicity/recovery story.  **Suggestion:** collapse into one ordered, partially-idempotent server commit endpoint.
3. **Category:** security  **Severity:** high  **Finding:** the write routes have no server-side validation independent of a prior client verdict call -- a caller could commit a proposal the verdict never covered.  **Suggestion:** validate server-side and bind the commit to the verdict's proposalDigest.
4. **Category:** robustness  **Severity:** medium  **Finding:** no overall subprocess deadline beyond the stdin-write timeout.  **Suggestion:** add one.
5. **Category:** concurrency  **Severity:** medium  **Finding:** the daemon-config existence check races its own lock's ensureFile.  **Suggestion:** move the existence check inside a non-ensureFile lock acquisition.

note: Round 2 (--mode iterate, mini-plan vs spec). Both legs revise, substantially overlapping. Every high-severity finding was adopted: charter.md missing from the first draft (both, high) -> now written by the commit endpoint; verdict's daemonConfig was client-assembled rather than a fresh server read (both) -> now server-side fresh-read-and-merge; the three writes were client-sequenced with no atomicity/recovery story (both) -> collapsed into one ordered, partially-idempotent server commit; write routes had no server-side validation independent of a prior verdict call (GLM, security) -> now validated server-side and bound to a proposalDigest; no overall subprocess deadline (GLM) -> added; daemon-config existence check raced its own lock's ensureFile (GLM) -> fixed; action->allowed_skills guessed from an id instead of the action catalog's slash_command field (openai) -> now reads that field; legacy non-kebab-case domains / Windows-path edge cases in the absolute-path guard (openai, low) -> both now explicit tested cases. No unresolved finding. A prior round-1 architecture-mode call (--mode architecture, verdicts GLM approve / openai revise, both raising the same wizard-vs-single-page-form proportionality concern, reconciled in favor of keeping the wizard per the card's explicit 'no new idiom' requirement) does not get its own row per this project's convention -- full text captured in the iterate spec's '## External / Architecture Review' section and plan_review_raw.md in this same directory.
